schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE INSURANCE (
    PID INT,
    TIV_2015 NUMERIC,
    TIV_2016 NUMERIC,
    LAT NUMERIC,
    LON NUMERIC,
    PRIMARY KEY (PID),
    CHECK (TIV_2015 >= 0),
    CHECK (TIV_2016 >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT ROUND(SUM(TIV_2016),2) TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE WHERE TIV_2015 IN (SELECT TIV_2015 FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY TIV_2015 HAVING COUNT(*)>1) AND (LAT,LON) IN (SELECT LAT,LON FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY LAT,LON HAVING COUNT(*)=1)
q2: WITH CTE AS(SELECT TIV_2015, COUNT(*) AS NUM FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY TIV_2015 HAVING COUNT(*) >=2), CTE2 AS(SELECT COUNT(PID) AS CNT, CONCAT_WS(',', LAT, LON) AS LOC FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY 2 HAVING COUNT(PID) = 1 ) SELECT SUM(TIV_2016) AS TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE WHERE TIV_2015 IN (SELECT TIV_2015 FROM CTE) AND CONCAT_WS(',', LAT, LON) IN (SELECT LOC FROM CTE2)

counterexample: INSERT INTO INSURANCE (PID, TIV_2015, TIV_2016, LAT, LON) VALUES (1, 1000, 500, 1.1, 2.2); INSERT INTO INSURANCE (PID, TIV_2015, TIV_2016, LAT, LON) VALUES (2, 1000, 500, 1.1, 2.2); INSERT INTO INSURANCE (PID, TIV_2015, TIV_2016, LAT, LON) VALUES (3, 1500, 750, 3.3, 4.4);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because they handle the conditions for TIV_2015 and (LAT, LON) differently. Q1 first filters on TIV_2015 and then on (LAT, LON), while Q2 first filters on (LAT, LON) and then on TIV_2015. This difference can lead to different results if there are policies that meet one condition but not the other.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have policies with the same TIV_2015 but different (LAT, LON) values, and policies with the same (LAT, LON) values but different TIV_2015 values. The policy that meets the TIV_2015 condition but not the (LAT, LON) condition in Q1 should not meet the (LAT, LON) condition but not the TIV_2015 condition in Q2.
